title: The Brain Paradox: Hidden Emotion Flashes Prove Zero Guilt
description:
Experimental Chronicle — Paul Ekman & Wallace Friesen (1969-1978): Frame-by-Frame Microexpressions, FACS & the 'Pinocchio Nose' Myth, grounded in Paul Ekman, Wallace V. Friesen (1969) (Psychiatry). Empirical findings show that in 1969 at UC San Francisco, Paul Ekman and Wallace Friesen analyzed 16mm clinical interview films frame by frame at 24 frames per second after a hospitalized patient ('Mary') later confessed she had been hiding acute despair behind a cheerful smile to win a weekend pass.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how amygdala, motor cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that played at normal speed, Mary looked convincingly upbeat; stepped frame by frame, a two-frame (1/12-second) flash of intense anguish broke across her brow and mouth before a polite social smile snapped over it.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Paul Ekman, Wallace V. Friesen (1969). Nonverbal Leakage and Clues to Deception †. Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1080/00332747.1969.11023575
- P Ekman (1988). Commentary by Paul Ekman. Journal of Social and Biological Systems. https://doi.org/10.1016/0140-1750(88)90003-6
- Santiago González Suárez, Abner Gilead Araujo Guedes, Alfredo Parteli Gomes, Victor Machado Alves et al. (2026). SEVENEBASIC: DETECCIÓN Y ANÁLISIS DE EXPRESIONES FACIALES ASOCIADAS A LAS SIETE EMOCIONES BÁSICAS DE PAUL EKMAN. LUMEN ET VIRTUS. https://doi.org/10.56238/levv17n58-033
